name: PostgreSQL
tagline: Durable SQL storage: WAL, streaming replicas, point-in-time backups, pooled connections.

howItWorks.title: WAL and checkpoints
howItWorks.body:
Changes are appended to the WAL and fsynced at commit.
Data files are written lazily; a checkpoint flushes dirty pages.
Crash recovery replays WAL from the last checkpoint.
wal_level, max_wal_size and synchronous_commit tune durability against I/O.

howItWorks.title: Streaming replication
howItWorks.body:
A standby pulls WAL from the primary's walsender.
Needs a REPLICATION role, max_wal_senders and a pg_hba replication rule.
pg_basebackup -R seeds the standby and writes standby.signal.
Replication slots retain WAL for a standby; a dead standby fills the disk.

howItWorks.title: Promotion
howItWorks.body:
pg_promote() ends recovery and starts a new timeline.
The old primary must be rewound with pg_rewind or rebuilt.
Plain Postgres does not fence it; Patroni or repmgr automates this.
Check pg_stat_replication replay lag before switching.

howItWorks.title: Backups and PITR
howItWorks.body:
pg_basebackup takes the physical base.
archive_command ships each WAL segment to S3-compatible storage.
restore_command plus recovery_target_time replays to a chosen moment.
An unrestored backup is not a backup; rehearse it.

howItWorks.title: Pooling and hardening
howItWorks.body:
PgBouncer transaction mode multiplexes clients onto few backends.
listen_addresses names the interfaces Postgres binds.
pg_hba.conf is first-match: type, database, user, CIDR, method.
ssl = on with scram-sha-256 protects credentials and data in transit.

howItWorks.title: What sits in front
howItWorks.body:
Platform services connect with libpq or a driver; the wire protocol runs on TCP 5432.
A pooler such as PgBouncer listens on 6432 and holds a small pool of backends.
A failover endpoint is a virtual IP or HAProxy health-checking Patroni's REST API on 8008.
libpq accepts several hosts; target_session_attrs=read-write finds the current primary.

howItWorks.title: What sits behind
howItWorks.body:
Behind the primary sit its disk, the WAL archive and the streaming standbys.
WAL archives and base backups go to object storage; pgBackRest and WAL-G are the usual tools.
On Kubernetes, an operator such as CloudNativePG manages primary, replicas and Services.
postgres_exporter exposes metrics to Prometheus; Grafana draws them.

howItWorks.title: Alternatives
howItWorks.body:
MySQL or MariaDB: choose them when the application or team already standardises on them.
Managed PostgreSQL (RDS, Cloud SQL): choose it to hand off backups and failover.
SQLite: a single-file embedded database for one-process tools and tests.
Distributed SQL such as CockroachDB: choose it for multi-region writes, at extra cost.

flow: The app connects to PgBouncer, which holds a few server connections.
The backend process parses and executes the transaction.
Changes are appended to the WAL and fsynced at commit.
The walsender streams WAL to the standby, which replays it.
archive_command copies each finished segment to S3-compatible storage.
Checkpoints flush dirty pages to the data files.
On primary failure, promote the standby to a new timeline.
Restore: base backup plus archived WAL to a target time.

deploy.summary: PostgreSQL 16 primary and standby on Ubuntu 22.04: hardened, TLS, WAL archiving to MinIO, PgBouncer.
prerequisites: An S3-compatible endpoint (MinIO) and bucket pg-wal
AWS CLI configured for the postgres user
SSH and network steps on both VMs

steps.title: SSH key login and sshd hardening
steps.code:
ssh-keygen -t ed25519 -C ops@workstation
ssh-copy-id ops@10.0.0.11
ssh ops@10.0.0.11 'sudo tee /etc/ssh/sshd_config.d/10-harden.conf' <<'EOF'
PasswordAuthentication no
PermitRootLogin no
KbdInteractiveAuthentication no
AllowUsers ops
EOF
ssh ops@10.0.0.11 'sudo sshd -t && sudo systemctl reload ssh'
steps.note: Test a second session before closing the first. 10.0.0.x is a placeholder.

steps.title: Static address and firewall
steps.code:
sudo tee /etc/netplan/60-static.yaml <<'EOF'
network:
  version: 2
  ethernets:
    ens18:
      dhcp4: false
      addresses: [10.0.0.11/24]
      routes:
        - to: default
          via: 10.0.0.1
      nameservers:
        addresses: [10.0.0.2]
EOF
sudo chmod 600 /etc/netplan/60-static.yaml
sudo netplan apply
sudo ufw allow from 10.0.0.0/24 to any port 22,5432,6432 proto tcp
sudo ufw --force enable
steps.note: Placeholders: interface, addresses, DNS. Add A records pg1.lab.local and pg2.lab.local.

steps.title: Install PostgreSQL 16
steps.code:
sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-common awscli
sudo /usr/share/postgresql-common/pgdg/apt.postgresql.org.sh -y
sudo apt-get install -y postgresql-16
pg_lsclusters
steps.note: Uses the official PGDG repository. Pin the minor version in production.

steps.title: Primary: listen, WAL, archive, TLS
steps.code:
sudo openssl req -new -x509 -days 365 -nodes -subj '/CN=pg1.lab.local' \
  -out /var/lib/postgresql/server.crt -keyout /var/lib/postgresql/server.key
sudo chown postgres: /var/lib/postgresql/server.* && sudo chmod 600 /var/lib/postgresql/server.key
sudo tee /etc/postgresql/16/main/conf.d/10-prod.conf <<'EOF'
listen_addresses = '10.0.0.11'
wal_level = replica
max_wal_senders = 5
max_replication_slots = 5
archive_mode = on
archive_command = 'aws s3 cp %p s3://pg-wal/pg1/%f --endpoint-url http://minio.lab.local:9000'
ssl = on
ssl_cert_file = '/var/lib/postgresql/server.crt'
ssl_key_file = '/var/lib/postgresql/server.key'
EOF
steps.note: A self-signed certificate is for the lab only; use your CA in production. Credentials live in ~postgres/.aws.

steps.title: Roles and pg_hba.conf
steps.code:
sudo systemctl restart postgresql@16-main
sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE ROLE replicator REPLICATION LOGIN PASSWORD 'CHANGE_ME'"
sudo -u postgres psql -c "CREATE ROLE app LOGIN PASSWORD 'CHANGE_ME'"
sudo -u postgres createdb -O app appdb
echo 'hostssl replication replicator 10.0.0.0/24 scram-sha-256' | sudo tee -a /etc/postgresql/16/main/pg_hba.conf
echo 'hostssl all app 10.0.0.0/24 scram-sha-256' | sudo tee -a /etc/postgresql/16/main/pg_hba.conf
sudo systemctl reload postgresql@16-main
steps.note: pg_hba.conf is first-match; keep specific CIDRs, never 0.0.0.0/0 with trust.

steps.title: Seed the standby and take a base backup
steps.code:
# on pg2: sudo systemctl stop postgresql@16-main && sudo rm -rf /var/lib/postgresql/16/main/*
sudo -u postgres PGPASSWORD=CHANGE_ME pg_basebackup -h 10.0.0.11 -U replicator \
  -D /var/lib/postgresql/16/main -R -X stream -C -S standby1 -P
sudo systemctl start postgresql@16-main
# on pg1: physical base backup to storage
sudo -u postgres pg_basebackup -D /tmp/base -Ft -z -X fetch && aws s3 cp /tmp/base s3://pg-wal/pg1/base --recursive --endpoint-url http://minio.lab.local:9000
steps.note: Set listen_addresses and ssl on pg2 too. Adapt the primary's conf.d file.

steps.title: Promote the standby
steps.code:
sudo -u postgres psql -h 10.0.0.12 -c 'SELECT pg_promote()'
sudo -u postgres psql -h 10.0.0.12 -c 'SELECT pg_is_in_recovery()'
# old primary: rejoin with pg_rewind or rebuild from a new base backup
steps.note: Fence the old primary first. Patroni or repmgr automates detection and fencing.

steps.title: PgBouncer
steps.code:
sudo apt-get install -y pgbouncer
sudo tee /etc/pgbouncer/pgbouncer.ini <<'EOF'
[databases]
appdb = host=10.0.0.11 port=5432 dbname=appdb
[pgbouncer]
listen_addr = 10.0.0.11
listen_port = 6432
auth_type = scram-sha-256
auth_file = /etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt
pool_mode = transaction
max_client_conn = 500
default_pool_size = 20
EOF
sudo -u postgres psql -Atc "select format('\"%s\" \"%s\"', rolname, rolpassword) from pg_authid where rolname='app'" | sudo tee /etc/pgbouncer/userlist.txt
sudo systemctl restart pgbouncer
steps.note: Transaction mode breaks advisory locks and session-level SET.

verify: sudo -u postgres psql -c 'SELECT client_addr,state,replay_lag FROM pg_stat_replication'
sudo -u postgres psql -c 'SELECT pg_is_in_recovery()'   # t on the standby
sudo -u postgres psql -c 'SELECT archived_count,failed_count FROM pg_stat_archiver'
psql 'host=10.0.0.11 sslmode=require user=app dbname=appdb' -c 'SELECT ssl FROM pg_stat_ssl WHERE pid=pg_backend_pid()'
pitfalls: A dead standby with a replication slot fills the primary's pg_wal.
A failing archive_command piles up WAL; watch pg_stat_archiver failed_count.
The old primary cannot rejoin without pg_rewind or a rebuild.
Transaction pooling breaks advisory locks, SET and session prepared statements.
The TLS key must be mode 0600 and owned by postgres.
trust or 0.0.0.0/0 in pg_hba.conf exposes the database.
Backups that are never restored are untested; rehearse PITR.
keyPoints: Every change hits the WAL before the data files.
Standbys replay streamed WAL and can be promoted to primary.
Base backup plus archived WAL gives point-in-time recovery.
A pooler caps backends so connection storms stay harmless.
quickDeploy: Harden SSH, set static addresses, open the firewall
Install PostgreSQL 16 and enable WAL archiving
Lock pg_hba.conf to hostssl and scram
Seed a standby, then promote it
osiNote: Wire protocol over TCP 5432, with TLS and scram authentication.
production: Size shared_buffers near 25% of RAM; keep max_connections low behind a pooler.
Run a streaming standby; fail over with Patroni or repmgr.
Archive WAL to S3-compatible storage; restore-test backups monthly.
Allow hostssl and scram only; bind listen_addresses to one interface.
Alert on replication lag, WAL disk usage and long transactions.
